name: HELLO
words: Says who is talking (used in the pairing proof)

name: NONCE
words: A fresh pairing challenge

name: AUTH
words: Pairs with the token in clear (this machine only)

name: AUTH-PROOF
words: Pairs by proof: HMAC-SHA256(token, nonce + name)

name: PING
words: Liveness and the clock exchange: OK PONG t1 t2 t3

name: STATE
words: The whole node as JSON (also pushed as STATE {…} on change)

name: CONTEXT
words: Show Bus §6 context: light, headline, items, commands, peers

name: HELP
words: The vocabulary, or one verb's syntax

name: VERBS
words: The vocabulary as JSON (name, syntax, words, risk, mutates)

name: SUBSCRIBE
words: Pushes STATE (and the other topics) on change, latest wins; EVENTS in order; MIRROR (paired only) is a primary's show to its hot backup

name: VIDEO PLAY
words: Plays on from where the clip holds (EXPECT refuses if the item changed under the key)

name: VIDEO PAUSE
words: Holds the clip where it is

name: VIDEO STOP
words: Back to the top and held (bare STOP is never a clip verb)

name: VIDEO RESTART
words: Plays from the top

name: VIDEO SEEK
words: Moves to a point, keeping play or hold

name: VIDEO END
words: Moves to n seconds before the end

name: VIDEO RATE
words: Playback speed

name: PLAYLIST LIST
words: Every playlist with its transport

name: PLAYLIST GET
words: One playlist, its items and transport

name: PLAYLIST NEW
words: Makes an empty playlist; answers its id

name: PLAYLIST ADD
words: Adds an item (media:…, generator:…, color:#…, playlist:… — another playlist's picture, never one that plays this one); answers its id

name: PLAYLIST REMOVE
words: Removes an item

name: PLAYLIST MOVE
words: Reorders an item

name: PLAYLIST DELETE
words: Deletes a playlist

name: PLAYLIST GO
words: Cues and plays an item (the next one when none is named); EXPECT refuses if the next item is not the one the key showed

name: PLAYLIST CUE
words: Loads an item and holds its first frame

name: PLAYLIST NEXT
words: Plays the next item

name: PLAYLIST PREV
words: Plays the previous item

name: PLAYLIST LOOP
words: Whether the list wraps to the top

name: PLAYLIST SYNC
words: Joins a sync group: the transport follows the group's leader

name: PLAYLIST FOCUS
words: The playlist the VIDEO verbs act on

name: PLAYLIST ANCHOR
words: A sync group leader's transport, taken exactly (leader to followers)

name: MEDIA LIST
words: The library with each item's availability

name: MEDIA GET
words: One item, its probe and where it is

name: MEDIA IMPORT
words: Adds a file or URL; hashes and probes it; answers its id

name: MEDIA REMOVE
words: Removes an item from the library (the file stays)

name: MEDIA HAS
words: Whether this node holds a file with that hash

name: MEDIA FETCH
words: Copies missing files (or one version of a clip) from a peer that has them

name: MEDIA STATUS
words: Transfers, readiness and disk

name: PATTERN
words: Puts a test pattern over the outputs, or once across a canvas wherever it is shown (OFF returns them to the show)

name: GENERATOR KINDS
words: Every generator kind with its parameters (grouped), traits, inputs and preset count

name: GENERATOR NEW
words: Makes a generator, optionally from a look; answers its id

name: GENERATOR SET
words: Sets a parameter (BY: a step for encoders)

name: OUTPUT LIST
words: Every output, its display and its health

name: DISPLAYS
words: The displays this machine sees

name: VIEW
words: A preview into the view's shared-memory ring on this machine: SHOW editor, output:<id>, projector:<id>, camera:<id> or scan:<id>:smart|confidence; DRAFT shows this session's blind draft instead of the air (editor only); CAMERA moves an editor view's eye; KEEP renews it (a view not renewed for 15 s is hidden); HIDE lets it go; SHARED <pid> shares the picture with that process on this machine as a GPU texture and its fences instead of the ring

name: OUTPUT ENABLE
words: Opens or closes an output

name: OUTPUT SOURCE
words: What a canvas or source output shows

name: OUTPUT IDENTIFY
words: Shows each output's name and number over its picture

name: BLACKOUT
words: Every output to black, and back

name: FREEZE
words: Every output holds its frame

name: SURFACE SOURCE
words: What a surface shows

name: SURFACE SHOW
words: Shows or hides a surface

name: PROJECTOR SOLVE
words: Solves pose (and lens) from the projector's pins

name: BLEND SOLVE
words: Computes the 3D blend maps from the projectors' coverage

name: WARP RESET
words: Takes an output's 2D warp back to rest

name: WARP NODE
syntax: WARP NODE <output> <column> <row> <dx> <dy> | WARP NODE <output> <c> <r> TO|BY <x> <y> PX
words: Moves one lattice node by dx, dy (normalised output units), or to or by x, y in the output's pixels

name: SCAN START
words: Structured-light scan of the projectors through the camera (INTO: another view of the same scan)

name: SCAN STATUS
words: The running scan's progress and quality

name: SCAN CANCEL
words: Stops a scan and gives the outputs back

name: SCAN APPLY
words: Turns a scan into mesh, projectors and surfaces

name: SCAN SURFACE
words: Makes a surface of what is at x, y (0–1 across and down the scan's smart-scan picture), or of a suggested region: its mesh faces and a mask outlining it; ON takes that projector's smart scan; answers its id

name: LATENCY MEASURE
words: Flashes white and times the camera's view of it

name: GET
words: Any entity as JSON

name: SET
words: Sets one field of an entity

name: ADD
words: Adds an entity; answers its id (an item, layer, mask, pin or fx slot names its owner first or as "parent" in the JSON)

name: REMOVE
words: Removes an entity

name: MOVE
words: Reorders an entity within its list

name: UNDO
words: Undoes the last edit

name: REDO
words: Redoes the last undone edit

name: PROJECT GET
words: The whole project as JSON

name: PROJECT SAVE
words: Saves the project

name: PROJECT OPEN
words: Opens a project (the show changes)

name: PROJECT NEW
words: A new project (the show changes)

name: NODES
words: The Show Bus peers this node hears

name: SYNC STATUS
words: Clock offset, jitter and the sync groups

name: SYNC LEAD
words: This node leads a sync group

name: SYNC FOLLOW
words: This node follows a sync group's leader

name: LINK PATTERNS
syntax: LINK PATTERNS <host[:port]>|OFF [<token>] | LINK PATTERNS FOLLOW-BLACKOUT ON|OFF
words: Follows a Patterns desk (its clip clock, its blackout); FOLLOW-BLACKOUT says whether the desk's blackout blacks this node out

name: LINK STAGEWATCH
words: Follows a Stagewatch (its timer as a source); "" follows the first one heard

name: PAIRING NEW
words: A new pairing token for this node: every paired peer pairs again (the token never rides a line — it is read where the node keeps it)

name: DEVICE LIST
words: Every projector link with what its projector reports: power, shutter, input, hours, faults

name: DEVICE GET
words: One link: what its projector reports, what its protocol can do and the plan PREPARE would run

name: DEVICE ADD
words: Links a projector box (pjlink, christie, panasonic, barco-pulse, sony-adcp, epson, nec); answers its id

name: DEVICE REMOVE
words: Forgets a projector link (the projector is left as it is)

name: DEVICE POWER
words: Powers a projector on, or to standby (OFF needs CONFIRM on an armed show)

name: DEVICE SHUTTER
words: Opens or closes a projector's shutter (AV mute)

name: DEVICE INPUT
words: Switches a projector's input, in its protocol's own words (31, HD1…)

name: DEVICE FREEZE
words: Holds a projector's picture

name: DEVICE PATTERN
words: Shows one of the projector's own test patterns, or none

name: DEVICE LENS
words: Drives a lens motor to a raw position or by steps, or recalls a lens memory

name: DEVICE RAW
words: Sends one line in the projector's own protocol (framing and authentication added)

name: DEVICE DISCOVER
words: Searches the network for projectors (the PJLink search; SWEEP also knocks on a /24)

name: DEVICE PREPARE
words: Readies a projector for a scan: shutter open, freeze and patterns off, its own geometry off, lens recorded

name: DEVICE IDENTIFY
words: Shows the projector's own identify pattern for a while

name: CREDENTIAL SET
words: Keeps a secret in this node's credential store (a projector link's password, the assistant's key); this machine only

name: CREDENTIAL CLEAR
words: Forgets a secret from this node's credential store; this machine only

name: CREDENTIAL LIST
words: Which references hold a secret on this node (never the secrets)

name: ASK
words: Asks the node's assistant; answers its words and every line it ran or queued

name: PROPOSALS
words: The assistant's lines waiting for a person (ALL: every proposal and how it ended)

name: APPROVE
words: A person approves a proposal: its line runs through the node's own checks

name: REJECT
words: A person rejects a proposal: it never runs

name: ASSISTANT STATUS
words: The assistant's settings: on or off, provider, model, effort, endpoint, what runs without asking, and whether a key is set (never the key)

name: ASSISTANT SET
words: Changes one of the assistant's settings, kept in the node's playmap.assistant.json and applied at once; from this machine or its paired desk only, never by an assistant. The key goes through CREDENTIAL SET assistant

name: SHOW
words: Show Mode: armed or rehearsal, by whom and since, the rules, the blind draft, panic, locks and the last preflight

name: SHOW ARM
words: Arms the show with no password: edits that would move the air are refused for every caller until SHOW DISARM; transport, blackout and PANIC stay live; armed survives a restart (ALL: every node of the group, answered with each member's receipt; refused while this node fans out to none)

name: SHOW DISARM
words: Back to rehearsal (ALL: every node of the group, answered with each member's receipt; refused while this node fans out to none)

name: SHOW SET
syntax: SHOW SET MINGO <ms> [ARMED|REHEARSAL] | REMOTE-VIEW-ONLY ON|OFF | DISARM-FROM PAIRED|DESK | EXPECT-ARMED ON|OFF | COMMIT-LEAD <ms> | PANIC-LEAD <ms>
words: Changes a show rule: double-GO protection, remote clients read-only while armed, who may disarm, warn when playing unarmed, how far ahead on the show clock a panic lands (COMMIT-LEAD waits for blind commits) (kept in the project, one undo step)

name: PANIC
words: Takes each output to its planned outcome over its fade, picture and sound, now or at an instant on the show clock; a second PANIC during the fade is the hard stop; HERE keeps it to this node; never refused for an operator (an assistant's PANIC waits for a person)

name: PANIC CLEAR
words: Brings the air back from a panic over a fade (transports stay as the outcome left them)

name: PANIC SET
words: Plans what PANIC does on an output, with its fade and the safe look SAFE shows (kept in the project, one undo step)

name: MASTER
words: The grand master over every output, picture and sound, faded on the show clock (not an undo step); HERE keeps it to this node

name: LOCK
words: Locks an entity or an area: no verb, undo or assistant changes it; playback and reading go on (not an undo step)

name: UNLOCK
words: Lifts a lock (ALL: every lock this show holds)

name: LOCKS
words: Every lock with who set it and why, and the areas an armed show adds

name: BLIND
words: The blind draft: whose, how many changes, when it commits

name: BLIND ON
words: Blind editing for this session: its edits go to a draft, off the air, until BLIND COMMIT

name: BLIND OFF
words: Leaves blind editing (refused while the draft holds changes: COMMIT or DISCARD them)

name: BLIND DIFF
words: What the draft changes, entity by entity, in field words, with conflicts

name: BLIND COMMIT
words: Lands the draft on the air as one undo step at a show boundary, frame-exact; FORCE overrides the conflicts it names

name: BLIND DISCARD
words: Drops the draft

name: PREFLIGHT
words: Checks the node is ready for the show from facts: outputs on present displays, media present and readable, linked projectors reachable and solved, free disk, the show clock, the links, the show's safety; each row carries the line that fixes it; answers the report's id (ALL: every node of the group, one section per node, refused while this node fans out to none; WAIT: answers with the finished report)

name: PREFLIGHT REPORT
words: The last preflight report, or one by id

name: HEALTH
words: This machine's health in one record: outputs, render, CPU, memory, disk, GPU, network, sync, devices, media (unknown is −1)

name: FLEET
words: Every PlayMap machine this node hears as one board in Patterns' Eye shape: lights by evidence, headline, problems

name: FLEET FOCUS
words: Focuses the board on a thing and its neighbours (a view, not journalled)

name: FLEET LENS
words: Shows one kind of thing on the board

name: FLEET NEXT
words: Focuses the next problem (reds, then ambers)

name: FLEET PREV
words: Focuses the previous problem

name: FLEET RESET
words: The board's view from before the focus

name: FLEET BACKUP
words: This node becomes a hot backup of a primary: it mirrors the primary's project, air and transports on its own outputs; FAILOVER makes it the primary

name: FLEET SOLO
words: This node stops backing up and plays on alone

name: FLEET PROMOTE
words: This node leads the group now, continuing the old leader's show clock without a step

name: FAILOVER
words: The backup takes the show from its primary and fences the old primary by epoch

name: FAILBACK
words: Hands the show back to the original primary (a person's press only)

name: FLEET ROUTE
syntax: FLEET ROUTE <output> DEVICE <device> <input> <backup input> | FLEET ROUTE <output> NONE | FLEET ROUTE TEST
words: What FAILOVER switches so the audience sees the backup: the projector's input, confirmed by its own answer; TEST reads reachability and the current input

name: OUTPUT STATS
words: Each output's presentation from the display's side: path, measured refresh, missed vblanks, held frames, latency, lock

name: PRESENT RESET
words: Zeroes presentation counters (the old totals go to the journal)

name: SYNC APPLY
words: The leader joins the group's outputs to the hardware framelock and answers each output's observed lock

name: SYNC LEAVE
words: Outputs leave the framelock and present free-running, measured

name: SYNC REJOIN
words: Outputs that fell out of the lock join it again (armed: only while blacked out)

name: PRESENT PATH
words: Where outputs present from the render host's next start: AUTO is OpenGL this round; D3D12 presents through Direct3D 12's flip presenters; DXGI (flip model on Windows) is experimental until proven on the machine (kept on the node)

name: SYNC RECEIPT
words: A group member's answer to an air line its leader fanned out (member to leader, on the member's anchor feed)

name: SYNC LATENCY
words: The group's air latency (AUTO: the largest output latency any member reports)

name: MEDIA INSPECT
words: What a clip is to the decoder: codec and texture, chunks, second stage, MB per frame and per second, HDR reading, odd size, and the lines that fix what is slow

name: DECODE STATUS
words: This node's decode paths: zero-copy ready, direct sampling proven, and every open decoder's path, why and cost

name: DECODE POLICY
words: The best path decoders opened from now on may take (open ones keep theirs); DIRECT on a D3D11 renderer needs a proof unless FORCE

name: MEDIA OPTIMISE
syntax: MEDIA OPTIMISE <media>…|ALL [TO hap|hap-alpha|hap-q|hap-q-alpha] [QUALITY FAST|SHOW] | MEDIA OPTIMISE CANCEL|PAUSE|RESUME [<job>|ALL]
words: Makes a version of clips that plays on the GPU here, in the background, never disturbing playback and never touching the source; CANCEL, PAUSE and RESUME steer jobs (a running job's pause or resume is accepted, pending, until its worker holds or goes on: the job's held in STATE)

name: MEDIA JOBS
words: Every optimise job and the governor's state

name: MEDIA VERSIONS
words: A clip's versions, which plays on this node and why

name: MEDIA USE
words: Which file a clip plays (from its next open, never mid-air)

name: MEDIA RULES
words: The optimise mode and quality, this show's rules, then the built-in table's rule names

name: MEDIA RULE
words: Changes the optimise mode: AUTO optimises clips imported from now on as the rules say, NEVER optimises nothing unless a person asks

name: INPUT LIST
words: Every live input with its health, its users and whether it is on air

name: INPUT DISCOVER
words: The NDI, OMT and Spout sources and the capture devices, with their modes, this node sees

name: INPUT ADD
words: Adds a live input (ndi:HOST (Name), omt:HOST (Name), omt://host:port, spout:Name, or a capture card's capture:<provider>/<device>[/<input>] in a MODE and FORMAT) to the library, received once however many surfaces show it; answers its id

name: INPUT FALLBACK
words: What an input shows when its feed is lost

name: INPUT BACKUP
words: A second feed the input takes over on loss

name: INPUT SWITCH
words: Switches an input between its feeds (answered at the first frame)

name: INPUT RECONNECT
words: Reconnects a stale or lost input (refused while it delivers)

name: SEND LIST
words: Every send with its tap, format, receivers, tally and drops

name: SEND ADD
words: Sends a picture to the network or to other apps on this machine: tap output:<id>, canvas:<id> or source:<ref>; answers its id

name: SEND ENABLE
words: Starts or stops a send

name: SEND REMOVE
words: Removes a send (its receivers lose the picture)

name: VIDEOIO STATUS
words: The NDI, OMT and Spout runtimes on this node: loaded, versions, discovery, bandwidth

name: VIDEOIO CHECK
words: Video I/O readiness rows with the lines that fix them

name: VIDEOIO SET
syntax: VIDEOIO SET NDI ON|OFF | NDI-GROUPS <groups> | NDI-DISCOVERY <host,…>|OFF | OMT ON|OFF | OMT-DISCOVERY <host[:port]>|OFF | SPOUT ON|OFF | MAX-SEND-MBPS <0-100000>
words: Changes this node's video I/O settings

name: CONTROL STATUS
words: Control input: OSC, MIDI and DMX, surfaces, bindings, learning

name: CONTROL PORTS
words: The MIDI ports and OSC, Art-Net and sACN sockets of this machine, and which surface each is

name: CONTROL MONITOR
words: The last inputs heard, raw and normalised, with the binding each fired

name: CONTROL PROFILES
words: The controller profiles (feedback, init and exit messages) and whether each is verified

name: CONTROL ENABLE
words: Every control input on or off (bindings pause; kept on the node)

name: CONTROL SURFACE
syntax: CONTROL SURFACE ADD <name> MIDI|OSC|ARTNET|SACN [<match>] [PROFILE <id>] | CONTROL SURFACE REMOVE <surface>
words: Names a controller the show's bindings use; answers its id

name: CONTROL ALIAS
words: Which port a surface is on this machine (kept on the node)

name: CONTROL FEEDBACK
words: An OSC client that hears the node's state

name: CONTROL DMX
words: Listens for Art-Net or sACN control input (off until turned on; kept on the node)

name: CONTROL INJECT
words: Fires the bindings of an input as if it moved (never from an assistant)

name: BIND LIST
words: The show's control bindings with their words, state and takeover

name: BIND ADD
syntax: BIND ADD <input words> TO <target line> | BIND ADD <json>
words: Binds a control input to a wire line ('*' carries the value: SET sf… opacity *); answers its id

name: BIND LEARN
syntax: BIND LEARN [FROM <surface>|MIDI|OSC|ARTNET|SACN] <target line> | BIND LEARN OFF
words: Binds the next control that moves to the target line (30 s); OFF stops learning

name: BIND FORGET
words: Forgets bindings by target or by input

name: BIND ENABLE
words: Turns a binding, or a surface's bindings, on or off

name: NUDGE
words: Moves a number by a step within its range (encoders, Companion dials)

name: TIMECODE STATUS
words: Timecode sources (rolling, format, speed, errors) and every playlist that chases one

name: TIMECODE DEVICES
words: The audio inputs, MIDI ports and Art-Net interfaces timecode can arrive on

name: TIMECODE SOURCE
syntax: TIMECODE SOURCE ADD <name> LTC [<device>[:<channel>]] [FORMAT <fmt>] | TIMECODE SOURCE ADD <name> MTC <port> [FORMAT <fmt>] | TIMECODE SOURCE ADD <name> ARTNET [STREAM <n>] [FORMAT <fmt>] | TIMECODE SOURCE ADD <name> INTERNAL [FORMAT <fmt>] | TIMECODE SOURCE REMOVE <source> | TIMECODE SOURCE RESET <source>
words: Adds, removes or resets a timecode input; answers its id

name: TIMECODE CHASE
words: A playlist follows timecode: each item at its TC in, locked to the code's fitted line, freewheeling through dropouts

name: TIMECODE ENGAGE
words: Engages or disengages a chase (disengaged, the playlist plays by hand from where it is)

name: TIMECODE SET
syntax: TIMECODE SET <playlist> DELAY <±ms> | TIMECODE SET <playlist> FREEWHEEL <ms> | TIMECODE SET <playlist> ONLOSS HOLD|STOP|CONTINUE | TIMECODE SET <playlist> JUMP <ms>|AUTO | TIMECODE SET <playlist> GAP BLACK|HOLD
words: Tunes a chase

name: TIMECODE IN
words: The timecode an item starts at (NOW takes the chase's current code)

name: TIMECODE INTERNAL
syntax: TIMECODE INTERNAL <source> PLAY|STOP | TIMECODE INTERNAL <source> LOCATE <tc> | TIMECODE INTERNAL <source> RATE <0.5-2>
words: Runs an internal timecode source (rehearsal or master)

name: INDEX
words: The show's structure for controllers (playlists and items, surfaces, projectors, outputs, devices, generators, and every package's section with its preset hint) with structure and label signatures

name: EVENTS
words: The node's recent events (item start and end, armed, panic, faults, calibration moved…) for automations

name: PRESENCE
words: A controller says what it is and what it shows (kind, module version, page)

name: WHOAMI
words: This session as the node sees it: transport, role, paired, armed, and the verbs it may run now

name: THUMB
words: A small picture for a key or a list, cached by content and ETag

name: FX KINDS
words: Every effect kind (built-in and this show's ISF files) with its parameters and traits

name: FX LIST
words: The effect chain of a layer, canvas, surface, output or playlist item, with each slot's state

name: FX ADD
words: Adds an effect to a chain (positions count from 1); answers its slot id

name: FX REMOVE
words: Removes an effect

name: FX MOVE
words: Moves an effect to a position in its chain (from 1)

name: FX SET
words: Sets an effect's parameter, mix, blend or scale

name: FX BYPASS
words: Bypasses effects (ALL ON is the panic outcome 'effects off')

name: FX RESET
words: Sets an effect's parameters back to their defaults

name: FX IMPORT
words: Adds an ISF effect to the show (content-addressed, carried with it); answers its asset id and the compile report

name: FX CHECK
words: Translates an ISF source for GLSL 3.30 and ES 3.00, compiles it on this node's context and reports its issues by line

name: AUDIO INPUTS
words: The sound inputs this node can listen to (devices, the system's sound, test signals)

name: AUDIO LISTEN
syntax: AUDIO LISTEN <input>|DEFAULT|SYSTEM|OFF [CHANNELS 1|1+2|3-4|M|S] [GAIN <dB>] [HERE] | AUDIO LISTEN TEST CLICK|SWEEP|NOISE|DRUMS [CHANNELS 1|1+2|3-4|M|S] [GAIN <dB>] [HERE]
words: Chooses what the show listens to (HERE: this machine only)

name: AUDIO GAIN
words: The listening gain

name: AUDIO STATUS
words: Levels, bands, the spectrum, onsets and the input's state

name: TEMPO STATUS
words: The beat clock: BPM, beat, bar, phrase, source, lock and confidence

name: TEMPO SET
words: Sets the tempo (or moves it by n BPM), one lead ahead or at AT

name: TEMPO TAP
words: A tap; two or more set the tempo

name: TEMPO RESYNC
words: Puts the beat, bar or phrase on now

name: TEMPO NUDGE
words: Moves the beat's phase, slewed over a bar

name: TEMPO HALF
words: Halves the tempo

name: TEMPO DOUBLE
words: Doubles the tempo

name: TEMPO SOURCE
words: Where the beat comes from: taps and SET, or detected from the sound

name: TEMPO METER
syntax: TEMPO METER <beats per bar 1-16> [<bars per phrase 1-64>]
words: The meter the bar and phrase sources count
forms: TEMPO METER <beats per bar 1-16> [<bars per phrase 1-64>]

name: MOD SOURCES
words: Every modulation source on this node (audio:, beat, bar, phrase, beat:pulse, bpm, lfo:) with its value and whether it is pure or live

name: MOD BIND
syntax: MOD BIND <entity> <param> <source> [AMOUNT <-1…1>] [OFFSET <x>] [MODE ADD|SCALE|REPLACE] [CURVE LINEAR|EASE|STEP|EXP|LOG|S] [SMOOTH <attack ms>[/<release ms>]] [RANGE <min> <max>] [STEPS <n>] [INVERT]
words: Modulates a number of a generator, layer, surface or effect slot from a source, live; the show keeps the base value
forms: MOD BIND <entity> <param> <source> [AMOUNT <-1…1>] [OFFSET <x>] [MODE ADD|SCALE|REPLACE] [CURVE LINEAR|EASE|STEP|EXP|LOG|S] [SMOOTH <attack ms>[/<release ms>]] [RANGE <min> <max>] [STEPS <n>] [INVERT]

name: MOD UNBIND
words: Removes modulation

name: MOD BYPASS
words: Holds every modulated number at its base value

name: MOD PEEK
words: The live value of each modulated number of an entity

name: GENERATOR GET
words: A generator with its effective values, bindings, inputs, morph, cost and state

name: GENERATOR RESET
words: Parameters back to their defaults

name: GENERATOR INPUT
words: A picture a generator reads (a particle flow emits where it is bright)

name: GENERATOR PRESETS
words: Curated and saved looks

name: GENERATOR RECALL
words: Applies a look (one undo step)

name: GENERATOR SAVE
words: Saves the generator's look in the show; answers its id

name: GENERATOR RETIME
words: Restarts a generator's own time (particles re-seed from that instant)

name: STING
words: Fires a sting every generator answers, on the show clock

name: STING CLEAR
words: Stops the sting

name: STING LIST
words: The sting presets

name: LED LIST
words: The LED rig: nodes, fixtures, pixels, universes, conflicts and bandwidth

name: LED NEW
words: Adds a fixture laid out on a space; answers its id

name: LED IMPORT
words: Imports pixel positions and patches from a CSV (one undo step)

name: LED PATCH
words: Patches a fixture to a node's universe and address (FORCE allows an overlap)

name: LED AUTOPATCH
words: Patches fixtures in order within each node's capacity

name: LED OUTPUT
words: This machine sends pixel data, or stops (one black frame first unless HOLD)

name: LED TEST
words: A test pattern on the LEDs instead of the show

name: LED LOCATE
words: Blinks one fixture

name: LED LEVEL
words: The LED rig's master level (live, not an undo step)

name: LED MONITOR
words: The bytes last sent to a universe, with the fixtures in it

name: SITE
words: The site frame: coordinate system, grid origin, rotation, scale and mains frequency

name: SITE ORIGIN
words: Sets the site frame; the whole stage moves with it in one edit

name: SITE MAINS
words: The venue's mains frequency

name: SITE POINTS
words: Imports surveyed control points; answers their ids and the lines it skipped

name: SITE CHECK
words: Measures the model against the control points: each point's distance and the fit

name: SURVEY IMPORT
words: Imports a surveyed model or point cloud (OBJ, PLY, glTF, LAS, E57, XYZ) into the site frame, off the control lane; answers its id

name: SURVEY LIST
words: Imported surveys with provenance and state

name: PROJECTOR PRIOR
syntax: PROJECTOR PRIOR <projector> THROW <ratio> [±<pct>] | PROJECTOR PRIOR <projector> AT <control> [±<m>] | PROJECTOR PRIOR <projector> AT <x> <y> <z> [±<m>] | PROJECTOR PRIOR <projector> CLEAR
words: What a solve may assume about a projector's lens and position

name: SITE GUIDE
words: The facade workflow as steps (survey, control points, pins, priors and solve, stacks, blend, score), each with its state and the line that does it

name: PLAN LIGHT
words: Predicted illuminance, luminance, contrast and pixel pitch per surface from the projectors as placed

name: STACK NEW
words: Groups projectors lighting one picture (the blend treats them as one); answers its id

name: STACK ALIGN
words: Fits each member's measured residual to the master's picture from a shared scan

name: STACK MATCH
words: Matches the members' colour gains from the scan's white frames

name: STACK FAILOVER
words: What the stack does when a member fails: hold the rest, or dim its blend group to match

name: STACK LIST
words: Stacks with members, residual, gains and degraded members

name: ALIGN NEW
words: Outputs aligned together through one camera onto one canvas; answers its id

name: ALIGN RUN
words: Measures the outputs through the camera and stages a correction (warp, blend and pedestal, γ, and with COLOR WHITE each white matched) with its score; ONLY scans those outputs again and keeps the others; nothing changes on the air until ALIGN ACCEPT

name: ALIGN STATUS
words: The running or last run

name: ALIGN SCORE
words: A run's score and every term with its words and fix

name: ALIGN CANCEL
words: Stops a run; the outputs are the show's again

name: ALIGN ACCEPT
words: Applies a staged run to its outputs as one edit; the corrections they had become their fallbacks

name: ALIGN REVERT
words: Back to each output's fallback correction

name: ALIGN CORNERS
words: The screen's corners in the camera picture (0–1), for an exact canvas

name: ALIGN CLEAR
words: Removes measured corrections from outputs; what they had becomes the fallback

name: DEVICE NATIVE
words: A projector's own geometry and edge blend, read live (Panasonic this round; others answer with words), for the double-correction guard

name: PHONE INVITE
words: A one-time link and QR code that makes a phone a scan camera (to this session only; never from an assistant)

name: PHONE LIST
words: Phones paired with this node and what their cameras can do

name: PHONE FORGET
words: Forgets a phone's key and disconnects it

name: SCAN NEXT
words: A folder camera in manual mode takes the picture of the pattern on the glass; any other camera has the pattern it waits on put up again and asked for afresh (a phone that was bumped or lost its view)

name: SCAN SUGGEST
words: Measured surface suggestions for a scan with their reasons, each queued as proposals only a person's APPROVE runs (SCAN SURFACE, and SURFACE QUAD for a plane); ASSISTANT: names and ranking from the node's assistant, from text only

name: SCAN SOLVE
words: Solves every projector, view and camera of a scan together (projector-anchored bundle adjustment); HOLD keeps those projectors at their stage poses

name: SCAN VIEWS
words: A scan's views with their residuals, tracks, pairing and state, and its coverage per projector

name: SCAN DROP
words: Drops a view from a scan and solves the rest again

name: LIGHT WALL
words: First light in one line: an output full screen on that display as a projector, with the edit overlay and the wall cursor on

name: SURFACE QUAD
words: Draws a surface as four corners in a projector's picture, clicked on the wall in any order; answers its id

name: SURFACE CORNER
syntax: SURFACE CORNER <surface> TL|TR|BR|BL|0|1|2|3 TO <x> <y> [PX|RASTER] | SURFACE CORNER <surface> <corner> BY <dx> <dy> [PX|RASTER]
words: Moves a quad's corner (BY: wall pixels by default)

name: SURFACE LATTICE
words: Gives a quad a lattice on top of its corners (its shape does not move)

name: SURFACE NODE
words: Moves a quad's lattice node

name: HANDLE SELECT
syntax: HANDLE SELECT <surface> TL|TR|BR|BL|<col>,<row> | HANDLE SELECT NONE | HANDLE SELECT <pin> | HANDLE SELECT <output> WARP TL|TR|BR|BL|<c>,<r> | HANDLE SELECT <output> MASK <i> <node>
words: The handle the wall shows enlarged and the arrows move: a quad's corner or lattice node, a pin, an output's warp corner or lattice node, or a mask's node

name: HANDLE NEXT
words: The next handle

name: HANDLE PREV
words: The previous handle

name: HANDLE NUDGE
words: Moves the selected handle (encoders and dials)

name: OVERLAY
words: The edit overlay on the wall, drawn through each output's warp; KEEP renews this session's lease (it lapses 15 s after the last)

name: CURSOR
words: This session's cursor on the wall (0–1 across the output)

name: CALIBRATION STATUS
words: Each projector's and output's score with its terms, current, fallback and staged results, and the running task

name: CALIBRATION HISTORY
words: Its results, newest first, with how far each moved the picture

name: CALIBRATION SAVE
words: Keeps the current calibration as a pinned result

name: CALIBRATION RECALL
words: Puts a kept result back (recorded as a new result)

name: CALIBRATION ACCEPT
words: Accepts the current (or a staged) result: it becomes the fallback

name: CALIBRATION FALLBACK
words: Back to the fallback result, exactly

name: CALIBRATION FORGET
words: Forgets a kept result (never the current, fallback or staged one)

name: CALIBRATION RESOLVE
words: Re-solves only the projectors named — from their pins as they stand, or with CAMERA from a fresh look at their dots (only the ones found moved) — scores and applies it (or stages it when it fails the gate); the others are not touched

name: CALIBRATION CANCEL
words: Stops a calibration task and gives the outputs back

name: MACHINE
words: This machine's identity, edition and support tier, the claims PlayMap made of Windows with what Windows answered, and any drift from the locked driver set, in words

name: MACHINE SET
syntax: MACHINE SET QOS HIGH|AUTO | TIMER HIGH|DEFAULT | MMCSS ON|OFF | PROCESS HIGH|NORMAL | CPUSETS AUTO|OFF | GPU-PRIORITY NORMAL|HIGH|REALTIME | GC DEFAULT|SHOW | AWAKE ON|OFF
words: Changes one of this machine's claims (power throttling, the timer, MMCSS, the process priority, CPU sets, the GPU scheduling class, the GC's show mode, keep-awake), kept on the node and applied now where Windows allows, else at the next start, saying which; REALTIME needs the privilege the installer grants

name: MACHINE LOCK
words: Keeps this machine's driver set (adapters, the Direct3D runtime, FFmpeg, the sync board's firmware, the OS build, PlayMap's build) as the one its shows run on, so preflight names any drift; CLEAR forgets it (kept on the node, never in the project)

name: GPU
words: The render device: its API, adapter, feature level and shader model, how its start went stage by stage, its epoch and its removals

name: GPU WARM
words: Makes every pipeline the show can reach now, off the render thread; WAIT answers when done, with how many were made, came from the cache and failed

name: GPU REHEARSE
words: Rehearses a device loss: removes the render device on purpose and answers when the first good frame is back, with the time (the outputs black for its length: refused while armed)

name: PRESENT PROVE
words: Measures each output's presentation over a window (10 s unless FOR) and answers its mode with the evidence: proven when the window met every vblank at the display's own rate, one frame from present to display

name: WATERMARK
words: A frame code on an output's picture at an edge or a place, at a block size, that an observer reads back to prove which frame was shown (one undo step)

name: OBSERVE
words: Watches an output's picture through a capture input (capture:<provider>/<device>[/<input>]) and reads its frame code: each frame shown, stale or lost; OFF stops watching (kept on the node)

name: OBSERVE STATUS
words: Each observed output's verdict, the frame seen and how late, in words

name: LATENCY STEP
words: Measures glass to glass: steps the frame code's region (VIA a camera, the whole output) to white and times when the observer or the camera sees each step, with each stage's share (it puts the steps on the air: refused while armed)

name: FX RELEASE
words: Lifts the quarantine on an effect kind whose shader took the GPU down, so its slots draw again (the quarantine is the node's, never a draft's)

name: UNDO LIST
words: The undo steps, newest first, in field words with who and when

name: UNDO TO
words: Undoes a step and every newer one as one action (UNDO TO the newest is one UNDO)

name: PIN MOVE
words: Moves a pin's picture point to or by x, y (0–1 across its projector's picture; PX: its pixels)

name: WARP CORNER
words: Moves a corner of an output's corner pin to or by x, y (PX: the output's pixels; NORM: 0–1 across it)

name: CANVAS SPAN
words: Spans a canvas across outputs as one edit: the outputs position by position (SIDE columns x rows, STACK outputs a position), the overlap between positions, each output's rectangle and edges, recorded as the span; over a rectangle a hand moved or a measured warp, refused naming each unless KEEP or REPLACE

name: CANVAS SOURCE
words: What a canvas shows as its base layer, fitted, filled or stretched

name: HAND
words: What a hand set over the automatic results: warp, blend, colour, masks and γ, each beside the measured value under it and the run that measured it

name: HAND CLEAR
words: Clears a hand's layer of an output, the measured layer under it staying (one undo step)

name: GUIDE
words: The guides as steps: LIST, every guide begun on this node; FLAT, WALL, OBJECT, FACADE or FIRST, one guide's steps for its subject, each with its state, words, facts and the automatic, hand and proposed lines

name: GUIDE BEGIN
words: Records a guide begun for its subject, with who and when

name: GUIDE END
words: Records a begun guide ended

name: GUIDE CHECK
words: A person marks a step they judged done (corners lined up by eye, a blend that looks right): the mark keeps the step's inputs and lapses once they move; never from an assistant's session

name: GUIDE UNCHECK
words: Takes a person's mark off a step; never from an assistant's session

name: VIEWPOINT FIT
words: Aims a viewpoint and fits its field of view to surfaces from its eye, with a margin, recorded as the fit; over an aim or field of view typed since, refused naming each unless KEEP or REPLACE

name: SURFACE MAP
syntax: SURFACE MAP <surface> UV | SURFACE MAP <surface> CANVAS <canvas> [<x> <y> <w> <h>] | SURFACE MAP <surface> PROJECTION FROM <viewpoint>
words: How a surface's content lies on it: by its own UVs, from a rectangle of a canvas, or projected from a viewpoint

name: OUTPUT PASSTHROUGH
words: Runs an output as its capture input's pass-through: one frame in flight, outside the delay ring, sampled as late as its measured render time allows
